atomicity.reason: One obligation - open the contactors above the temperature limit; the second sentence only scopes that same obligation per sensor.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained - trigger, scope and reaction are all stated without needing an adjacent requirement.

feasibility.reason: A limit comparison on an existing temperature acquisition path; consistent with the derating requirement, whose permitted power reaches zero at the same 60 C.

parent_fit.reason: Directly delivers the parent story's promise that the pack removes itself from the high-voltage circuit as soon as a cell leaves its safe temperature window.

unambiguity.reason: One reading: the explicit per-sensor scope removes the usual 'any versus all' question, and the strict 'above 60 C' fixes the boundary.

verifiability.reason: Threshold (60 C), scope (each temperature sensor individually) and the observable reaction (contactor-open command) are all concrete, so a bench test is a direct pass/fail.

summary: Crisp, testable overtemperature protection requirement; no axis-level defect found. Set-level note: no requirement defines what makes a cell TEMPERATURE measurement valid (the plausibility requirement covers voltages only), so the 'valid' qualifier in the trigger rests on project context.
